text:
anna: Heads-up — I'm drafting a small RFC to standardize how we link logs/metrics/traces across Redwood services. Current state is messy: different keys, languages, and some services rely on OTEL collector to add context.
tariq: +1. Can you outline the two main approaches you're considering? manual injection vs collector enrichment?
maria: For context, our console expects a single clickable id to jump from a trace to logs. Right now that only works reliably for ~60% of requests.
anna: Exactly. Option A: require every service to emit structured JSON logs with a consistent field name (my vote: `trace.trace_id`). Option B: rely on OTEL collector's logcorrelation processor to attach trace/span ids server-side.
kevin: Collector approach is tempting — less app change. But we had issues with older collector versions dropping attributes under high load. Also, not every language/runtime flows tracecontext into logs automatically.
julie: Agree. In Python we can add a logging Filter that injects trace id from contextvars. Very small patch. Example:
```python
import logging
from opentelemetry.trace import get_current_span
class TraceIdFilter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record):
        span = get_current_span()
        record.trace_trace_id = span.get_span_context().trace_id if span else None
        return True
```
Then update our JSON formatter to include `trace.trace_id`.
anna: Nice snippet. Proposal in RFC: prefer app-level injection (explicit field) for new services, but provide collector-backed backfill for older services for 6 months.
tariq: Concern: adding trace id as top-level string in logs increases cardinality for our log index. We should decide whether it's an indexed label or just part of the JSON payload. Indexing many unique trace ids will blow up costs.
maria: Console linking only needs to parse trace id from log payload — not index it. So default should be non-indexed. We'll add a separate thin index for debug workflows (opt-in) for a few services.
kevin: Also need to document exact key names. Variants we've seen: `trace_id`, `traceId`, `trace.trace_id`, `otel.trace_id`. Picking something consistent matters for search and dashboards.
anna: RFC will standardize on `trace.trace_id` and `trace.span_id` to avoid collisions and hint at nesting. The telemetry team (devx) will add parsers for other historical keys during transition.
devx: We can make the console detection layer resilient: try common keys, then fallback to OTEL-extracted context. But I'd rather we standardize sooner than later.
julie: Rollout plan idea: 1) update logging lib templates + template PR in infra-templates. 2) opt-in canary in staging (10 services) with collector enrichment enabled. 3) monitor trace->logs link success rate and cost delta. 4) full rollout.
anna: For metric/traces retention interaction: if we sample 90% of traces, logs will still have trace ids for unsampled traces and links won't lead to traces. We should surface that in UI (e.g., "trace not sampled").
tariq: Good call. We also need to adjust sampling policies for high-throughput endpoints used in experiments so that dev teams can correlate when needed.
kevin: On the collector side, there's a config we can add to enrich log records with trace/span ids before exporting. Example OTEL config fragment:
```yaml
processors:
  batch:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: trace_id
        action: insert
        value: "%{trace_id}"
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      processors: [attributes]
```
This needs testing across gRPC/HTTP exporters.
maria: Also flagging security: trace ids can be PII-adjacent if teams dump full user identifiers in trace attributes. We should ensure our log sanitation pipeline runs after correlation.
anna: Right — add a step in RFC: ensure `log-sanitizer` runs post-correlation and fails builds if disallowed keys appear.
devx: I'll prototype a small collector transform that normalizes incoming keys and writes a `trace.trace_id` field from either OTEL context or existing log key aliases.
julie: Can we also make the console support jumping to logs filtered by `trace.trace_id` across multiple tenants/regions? We need to avoid leakage between customers.
kevin: Tenant isolation is handled by the `customer_id` label in logs. Console query will include tenant filter + trace id.
maria: Ops ask: let's add a dashboard to track (a) % of requests with a linkable trace, (b) added log size delta, (c) cost delta of indexing. We'll gate rollout until link rate > 95% and cost delta < 8%.
anna: Sounds good. I'll file the RFC today and include a migration checklist and canary playbook. Any objections to the `trace.trace_id` naming? speak now.
tariq: No objection. +1 from infra side.
kevin: +1 from runtime. Will schedule a quick test with the collector team tomorrow.
maria: +1 from console. I'll add UI text for unsampled traces.
anna: Thanks everyone. I'll post RFC link when ready. sla-bot: scheduled `telemetry-rfc` review for 2026-04-12 16:00.
sre-bot: Deployed collector prototype to staging (collector-2026-03-18). Monitor `collector.errors` for 2 hrs.
kevin: Noted — will watch. If we see attr drop, collector approach is back to the drawing board.
anna: RFC link: <https://redwood.internal/rfcs/telemetry-correlation-1769951234> (draft). Feedback welcome in-thread or PRs on the doc.
maria: Quick follow-up: please add a tiny changelog item for SDKs so dev teams know how to enable the TraceIdFilter.
julie: I'll add the infra-templates PR and ping teams for a 2-week window to opt into the canary.
anna: Closing for now. We'll reconvene after the collector test tomorrow. :thumbsup:
